exposure: Implementation of an Enhanced Recovery After Cesarean Delivery (ERAS-CD) pathway
Standardization of opioid discharge prescriptions to <=25 tablets of 5 mg oxycodone
outcome: Inpatient opioid consumption (median morphine milligram equivalents)
Patient-reported pain scores (at discharge and one week post-discharge)
cohort: The study participants were women who underwent cesarean delivery at a single, urban academic hospital, surveyed both before and after the implementation of an ERAS-CD pathway.
finding: Implementing an ERAS-CD pathway was associated with a significant decrease in inpatient and postdischarge opioid consumption while improving pain control after cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: The ERAS-CD pathway specifically for cesarean delivery patients was associated with reduced opioid consumption and better pain control, demonstrating a positive impact on the experience of birth via cesarean section.
followup_time: 5 to 8 days after discharge (for opioid use) and 1 week after discharge (for pain scores)
